This plot is my sorghum, here in Mtwara. The soil is sandy and I have no money for fertilizer from the shop — sorghum is what I plant because it survives when rains are poor. I use my own seed from last season, same as my father did, and I intercrop with cowpea or cassava so we have food even if one crop fails. My wife and I do the weeding by hand hoe; if weeds come heavy I may call a neighbor for a few days during weeding.
